Type.evidence_source: [/page/3/Text/8] The study took place in London, UK. Individuals aged 65 or over were eligible for inclusion in the study if they had been in contact with the local mental health services following an attempt within the previous five days to 20 weeks, with most under four weeks. Exclusion criteria were cognitive impairment (a MMSE score of524), psychotic symptoms, and euthanasia-driven attempts. Since the method used in an attempt is often incongruent with the intent, no inclusion or exclusion criteria were set with regard to method. During the study recruitment period, mental health practitioners referred all individuals who they had clinically identified as having made an attempt. No objective measures of suicidal intent were administered as participants were identified after their attempt. All participants had indicated having an intention to die at some point during the clinical assessment procedure. Twenty-one individuals meeting the inclusion criteria were identified, and 15 (71%) agreed to participate.

[/page/3/Text/9] All participants had been diagnosed by a psychiatrist as being depressed at the point of the attempt, retrospectively or according to a pre-existing record. [/page/3/Text/10] Twelve of the 15 attempts were deemed to be of serious intent by a clinician, with the remaining three being less clear.
